rv.q: Alan Strachan’s cleverly orchestrated revival of his second big hit, first seen in Scarborough in 1969, reminds us just what a comic master Ayckbourn is.
Strachan directs with precision and his exemplary cast respond with perfect nuance and comic nous.
Even so, the performances are an across-the-board triumph, and if half the new plays hitting our stages at the moment were half as accomplished, what a wonderful world this would be.
This is a triumphant return of an outstanding farce: vintage Ayckbourn, classic production.
There's not a lot to fault with this play. The writing is funny, although not hilarious, and the actors are excellent.

cn.t: Critics unanimously praise this Ayckbourn revival as a masterclass in comic timing and class satire. Strachan's sharp direction and the play's ingenious overlapping structure earn strong marks across the board.
